title: Responder Succession Playbook and Simulated Incident Catalog
author: Jordan Lee
content:
Overview

This playbook documents our responder succession model, a compact runbook index for frequently occurring incident classes, and a catalog of targeted game-day simulations to exercise succession handoffs, escalation behavior, and customer communications. It is intended to be a single-page operational reference for primary/secondary responders, incident commanders (ICs), and engineering managers during on-call shifts and planned exercises.

Scope

- Applies to Redwood Inference services running in production (hosted API, Dedicated control plane, and Private control plane).
- Covers responder succession, documented runbook links for service classes, escalation thresholds, status page and customer-comm templates, and a simulation catalog.
- Does not replace service-specific runbooks; it indexes them and prescribes succession/handoff discipline.

Responsibilities and roles

- Primary Responder: First on the signal. Responsible for initial triage, mitigation, and engaging Secondary if needed.
- Secondary Responder: Subject-matter cover for deeper investigation or sustained remediation. Takes over if Primary is unavailable > 30 minutes.
- Incident Commander (IC): Coordinates cross-team activity, customer notices, and post-incident actions once incident is declared.
- Engineering Manager: Ensures succession and backfills for prolonged incidents (> 8 hours).
- Communications Owner: Drafts and posts status page updates and customer emails. Usually IC or SRE on-call.

Succession rules (quick reference)

1. Alert -> Acknowledge
   - Primary must acknowledge within 5 minutes for P0/P1, 15 minutes for P2. If no ack, escalation page to Secondary at +5 (P0/P1) or +20 (P2).
2. Escalation -> Secondary takeover
   - If Primary cannot commit to active mitigation within 30 minutes, Secondary assumes active responder duties. Primary documents state and handoff directly in the incident channel and Incident Timeline.
3. IC appointment
   - If incident affects customer-facing SLOs or > 3 services, an IC must be named within 15 minutes of escalation to Secondary.
4. Manager involvement
   - If incident extends > 8 hours, Engineering Manager must be engaged and confirm a rotation/backfill plan.

Runbook index (service class, primary checklist, critical thresholds)

- API Gateway / Edge (service name: edge-proxy)
  - Primary checklist: Verify upstream health, throttle rules, recent deploys, TLS cert expiry.
  - Critical thresholds: 5xx rate > 1% sustained for 5m, latency p95 > 800ms for 5m.
  - Quick mitigations: Toggle degraded-mode routing, increase replicas, apply circuit-breaker.
  - Link: confluence://eng-platform/edge-proxy-runbook (use local link to service runbook)

- Serving Runtime (service name: runtime-orchestrator)
  - Primary checklist: GPU health, queue depth, KV cache errors, recent kernel rollouts.
  - Critical thresholds: queue depth > 200 per shard, worker OOM spikes, sustained token drop rates.
  - Quick mitigations: Drain pods, pin older model variant, increase batch deadline.
  - Link: confluence://eng-serving-runtime/runtime-orchestrator-runbook

- Auth & Billing (service name: auth-billing-api)
  - Primary checklist: Token validation, billing ingestion lag, quota enforcement.
  - Critical thresholds: billing pipeline lag > 15m, token error rate > 0.5%.
  - Quick mitigations: Fallback to last-known-good quotas, patch gating, temporary toggle of strict checks.
  - Link: confluence://finance-and-legal/auth-billing-runbook

Escalation matrix (condensed)

- P0 (system-down customer-impacting)
  - Primary ack: 0–5m
  - Secondary alert: +5m
  - IC: +15m
  - Manager: +60m or earlier if customer escalation requested
- P1 (severe degradation)
  - Primary ack: 0–5m
  - Secondary alert: +10m
  - IC: +30m
  - Manager: +4h
- P2 (partial loss / internal)
  - Primary ack: 0–15m
  - Secondary alert: +20m
  - IC appointment optional

Handoff checklist (use at every succession)

1. Post current state: concise bullets (what's broken, scope, last observed good timestamp).
2. Articulate next steps and blockers.
3. Confirm access and runbook links.
4. Confirm who will own customer comms.
5. Update Incident Timeline and Status Page draft.

Status page and customer comms templates

- Status page update (short form)
  - Title: [MAJOR] Degraded API performance in us-west-2
  - Impact: Customers in us-west-2 may see increased latency and request errors when generating text.
  - Current status: Investigating (IC: Jordan Lee)
  - Mitigation in progress: Rolling rollback of runtime kernel 3.4.1 -> 3.3.9 in us-west-2
  - Next update: 30 minutes

- Customer email template (initial)
  - Subject: Incident impacting Redwood API performance (us-west-2)
  - Body: Hello {{CustomerName}},
    We are currently investigating an issue affecting API latency for some requests in the us-west-2 region. Our engineers are actively diagnosing and mitigating. We will provide updates via our status page and directly every 30 minutes until resolved. If you require additional assistance, contact support@redwood.example with severity information.
  - Signature: Redwood Inference Support Team

- Customer email template (resolution)
  - Subject: Resolved: Redwood API performance incident (us-west-2)
  - Body: Hello {{CustomerName}},
    The incident affecting API latency in us-west-2 has been resolved as of {{ResolvedAt}}. Root cause: defective kernel rollout that increased queue latency under certain sequence-length patterns. Actions taken: rollback to kernel 3.3.9 and expanded canary checks for future rollouts. Postmortem with timeline and impact will be shared in 48 hours. We apologize for the disruption.

Post-incident actions and SLA checks

- Within 24 hours: IC publishes timeline and immediate mitigation summary to Incident Timeline.
- Within 48–72 hours: Designated author (IC or assigned engineer) drafts the postmortem using the standard template and assigns owners for follow-ups.
- SLA verification: Confirm measured downtime/latency against customer SLOs and billing adjustments pipeline.
- Root cause analysis: Link metrics (traces, logs, perf artifacts) to the postmortem and tag related change IDs.

Game-day / simulation catalog (title, objective, participants, success criteria)

- Simulation: "Succession Handoff Under Pager Storm"\  
  Objective: Exercise Primary->Secondary handoff when multiple P0s arrive during a single shift.\  
  Participants: 2 on-call engineers (primary/secondary), 1 IC, 1 communications owner.\  
  Injects: Two independent P0 alerts for edge-proxy and runtime-orchestrator within 7 minutes.\  
  Success criteria: Both incidents acknowledged, secondaries engaged within defined windows, at least one IC declared and status page updated within 20 minutes.

- Simulation: "Long Duration Backfill and Rotation"\  
  Objective: Validate manager-driven backfill and mid-incident rotation after 8 hours of active response.\  
  Participants: Primary, Secondary, Engineering Manager, Relief Engineer.\  
  Injects: Sustained incident requiring continuous mitigation and customer comms for 9 hours.\  
  Success criteria: Clean handover documented, no regression introduced during rotation, customer comms uninterrupted.

- Simulation: "Status Page & Comms Stress Test"\  
  Objective: Ensure Communications Owner can craft clear customer updates under pressure and with partial data.\  
  Participants: IC, Communications owner, Product PR.\  
  Injects: Conflicting telemetry and partial rollback attempt.\  
  Success criteria: First public notice within 15 minutes, consistent messaging across teams, and a resolved-status message within agreed SLA.

Simulation cadence and governance

- Run at least one simulation per quarter per SRE/Platform on-call squad.
- Quarterly leadership debrief and action-tracking for improvements.
- Maintain a simulation backlog prioritized by risk: kernel rollouts, capacity blips, auth/billing regressions.

Runbook hygiene and ownership

- Each runbook referenced must include: owner, last-tested date, linked playbook for rollback, and a minimal reproducible example (if applicable).
- Owners must schedule a runbook validation exercise at least once every 6 months or after any related release.

Checklist for postmortem and follow-ups

1. Timeline assembled and validated by primary/secondary.
2. Impact quantified (customer list, duration, requests affected).
3. Root cause and contributing factors documented.
4. Action items with owners and due dates.
5. Quality check: postmortem reviewed by a cross-functional reviewer within 72 hours.

Quick commands and artifacts to gather (examples)

- Recent deploys (last 2 hours): 
  kubectl get rs -n production -l app=edge-proxy --sort-by=.metadata.creationTimestamp
- Queue depth snapshot: curl -sS http://metrics.internal/api/query?metric=queue.depth&service=runtime-orchestrator
- Top 50 5xx traces (trace IDs): query tracing system with timeframe.

Appendix: Useful links and templates

- Incident Timeline template: confluence://oncall-and-incident-response/incident-timeline-template
- Postmortem template: confluence://oncall-and-incident-response/postmortem-template
- Runbook ownership register: confluence://oncall-and-incident-response/runbook-owners-register

Revision history

- 2024-04-11: Added simulation catalog and escalation timing updates (reviewers: Priya Nair).
